newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker activity remains sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker activity remains sluggish.

text.p: The Middle Eastern dirty tanker market continued its lacklustre performance on Thursday with a only a couple of VLCCs concluded, shipbrokers said
Other lifting sectors saw fair activity and mostly unchanged rates.
Brokers said that VLCC trips to Japan out of the Middle East settled at last done levels of W57.5, whilst trips westwards could command W48. VLCCs bound for Asia remained around W54.5.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med stayed around W92.5-95 as evidenced by Esso's chartering of the Centaur at that rate.
In the inter-UKC sector rates slipped fractionally to W92.5 off W1.5 from Wednesday.
A single transatlantic trip was seen with Bayway chartering the 80,000 tonner Freja Svea travelling N.Sea-New York.
Caribbean rates for 70,000 tonners heading upcoast U.S. rose to about W145-W148.
"This market is the strongest, globally. There are few vessels around, and there will be fewer by the end of the week. We should see rates rise five Worldscale points or so," a broker said.
